findings.title: The governed exporter has no enable path; its governance is unproven and its documented operational story is not implemented
findings.recommendation: Record in documentation/limitations.md that the adapter is present but not wired, and name the owner seam (tamoz-agent runtime-directory observability configuration) plus the authorization input that must gate enabling export. Do not build an enable path in this read-only package and do not add a plugin API (ADR-044 forbids it).

findings.title: The exporter applies no content/redaction policy to exported attributes and does not carry the governing policy digest
findings.recommendation: At the existing resource_spans seam, carry the document's policy_digest into the exported span (span attribute or resource block) so exported evidence is self-describing. Do not duplicate the redaction decision in the exporter; the upstream ContentPolicy already owns it.

findings.title: Export outcome and divergence are unrecorded; the exported span loses outcome, making a failed turn indistinguishable from a successful one
findings.recommendation: Emit tamoz.telemetry.export with its outcome attribute from the existing delivery_result seam, which already receives the result on every delivery attempt. Leave divergence accounting to the slice that owns the durable reader.

findings.title: AsyncExporter hardcodes a 2 s export deadline, silently overriding a longer configured timeout_ms
findings.recommendation: Pass the policy's own timeout at async_exporter.rb:75 instead of the literal 2_000, so the export deadline has exactly one source.

findings.title: Emitted span attributes are not OTLP/JSON-conformant; the exporter never validates its own wire body
findings.recommendation: At resource_spans, map attribute values into OTLP's typed AnyValue form and drop the whole batch locally with :rejected if any value cannot be represented.

findings.title: ADR-044 requires a conformance suite for the exporter adapter; no conformance suite exists
findings.recommendation: If a second adapter is planned, add the shared assertion set to exporter.rb and call it from test/otel_test.rb; until then record the ADR/code divergence in documentation/limitations.md.

findings.title: The documented OpenTelemetry gen_ai attribute mapping does not exist in code
findings.recommendation: Align the one-line table entry in documentation/design/observability.md:12 with what shipped, or track the mapping as planned work. No code change.

blind_spots: Sampling does not exist in either gem; limitations.md:126 is accurate. Because every accepted batch is exported and every refusal is counted only in memory, a collector's view of a turn cannot be distinguished from a complete one, and queue_full / post-disable losses are invisible to the collector. That misreading risk is worse than a sampled trace, which at least declares a rate.
Did not read metrics.rb, trace.rb, producer.rb, usage.rb end to end (belong to F15).
No live TLS collector was constructed, by instruction; HTTP behavior was verified against a blackhole address and by reading the Net::HTTP configuration. No bytes were sent to any real endpoint.

Could not verify whether an operator-facing OTLP configuration key exists outside the globs searched (*.rb, *.gemspec, *.yaml, *.yml, *.json, *.md, Gemfile, Rakefile). If one exists in a non-Ruby entry point, the no-enable-path conclusion needs revisiting; no candidate was found.

allow_local authority (egress_policy.rb:16) and the skipped post-resolution guard when it is true (:36) are recorded as observations, not findings: no authority contract for that flag was found and the path is unreachable.

rake ci / rake ci_full were not run (excluded by the brief). AsyncExporter queue bound, drop accounting, backoff, failure-limit disable and close path have no test; they were exercised only by ad hoc probes for this audit.
coordinator_flags: needs independent challenge: F16-SEC-02 and F16-OBS-01 (both major, high confidence)

F16-SEC-02 graded major rather than critical: no live leak occurs today because ContentPolicy keeps prompt text in the separate content field (signal.rb:129) and the gem is unreachable (F16-SEC-01); confirm that reasoning in challenge
F16-SEC-01 is a documentation/ownership gap, not a code defect; the off-by-default property itself is verified PASS and the gem is unreachable rather than merely disabled

verified passes to record: no production gem depends on tamoz-otel (only Gemfile:35 dev path line); bounded queue with counted drops and failure-limit disable; connect and read timeouts both set; redirects, proxy env and private addresses refused; resolved addresses re-validated and pinned against DNS rebinding; credential newline injection refused
documented gen_ai mapping (F16-COR-02) is absent from code but asserted in three design docs
